info: This is the master music_terms file
help: RCM Levels 5, 6 and 7 music terms. The level is the RCM level the term was introduced. The terms for a given level also include all the terms in previous levels.

tempo.name: allegretto
tempo.definition: fairly fast, a little slower than allegro

tempo.name: allegro
tempo.details: Cheerful or brisk; but commonly interpreted as lively, fast

tempo.name: andante
tempo.definition: moderately slow; at a walking pace

tempo.name: larghetto
tempo.definition: fairly slow, but not as slow as largo

tempo.name: rhubato
tempo.definition: with some freedom of tempo to enhance musical expression

dynamics.name: sforzando, sf, sfz
dynamics.definition: sudden strong accent of a single note or chord

structure_form.name: binary form
structure_form.details: These sections are often repeated, Uppercase letters A and B used to labelthese larger sections. Often unfold within a 16-measure structure

structure_form.name: contrasting period
structure_form.definition: new melodic material is introduced at the start of the second
structure_form.details: phrases denoted as a and b, 4 measures each, a ends with a half cadence, a1 ends with an authentic cadence

structure_form.name: deceptive cadence
structure_form.definition: cadence from V to any chord other than the tonic, usually the submediant (VI)
structure_form.details: also known as an interrupted or false cadence

structure_form.name: development
structure_form.definition: middle section of sonata form where themes are developed

structure_form.name: exposition
structure_form.definition: first section of sonata form, main themes are stated; often two contrasting themes

structure_form.name: form
structure_form.definition: overall structure of framework of a composition

structure_form.name: half cadence
structure_form.definition: cadence ending on the dominant triad

structure_form.name: parallel period
structure_form.definition: melodic material used in the first phrase is repeated at the start of the second
structure_form.details: phrases denoted as a and a1, 4 measures each, a ends with a half cadence, a1 ends with an authentic cadence

structure_form.name: perfect authentic cadence
structure_form.definition: V-I progression where both cords are in root position

structure_form.name: period
structure_form.definition: question-answer phrase pair; 2 phrases, 4 measures each

structure_form.name: primo, prima
structure_form.definition: first; upper part of a duet

structure_form.name: recapitulation
structure_form.definition: third and final section of sonata form, return of main themes stated in the exposition

structure_form.name: scale degrees
structure_form.definition: tonic, supertonic, mediant, subdominant, dominant, submediant, leading tone or subtonic, tonic

structure_form.name: secondo, seconda
structure_form.definition: second; second or lower part of a duet

structure_form.name: sonata form
structure_form.definition: Classical era form consisting of 3 sections: exposition, development, recapitulation

structure_form.name: cadence
structure_form.definition: end of a phrase in which the melody or harmony creates a sense of full or partial resolution

performing_instructions.name: simile
performing_instructions.definition: continue in the same manner as has just been indicated

performing_instructions.name: tre corde
performing_instructions.definition: three strings; release the left pedal

performing_instructions.name: una corde
performing_instructions.definition: one string; depress the left pedal

performing_instructions.name: volta
performing_instructions.example: prima volta: first time, seconda volta: second time

character_style.name: ad libitum, ad lib.
character_style.definition: at the liberty of the performer

character_style.name: D.C. al fine
character_style.definition: repeat from beginning to the end, or up to the word Fine

character_style.name: morendo
character_style.details: dying away in dynamics, and perhaps also in tempo

character_style.name: smorzando, smorz.
character_style.details: usually interpreted as a drop in dynamics, and very often in tempo as well

character_style.name: sonore
character_style.details: giving out a deep, resonant sound

signs.name: breath mark
signs.definition: take a breath, and/or slight pause or lift

signs.name: down bow
signs.definition: on a bowed instrument, play the note while drawing the bow downward

signs.name: glissando, gliss.
signs.definition: continuous slide upward or downward between two or more pitches

signs.name: repeat sign
signs.definition: repeat the music within the two signs, or between the sign and the beginning of the piece

signs.name: slur
signs.sign: arc connecting a group of notes

signs.name: tie
signs.definition: hold for the combined values of tied notes

signs.name: up bow
signs.definition: on a bowed instrument, play the note while drawing the bow upward

modify_link_terms.name: ma
modify_link_terms.example: ma non troppo: but not too much

modify_link_terms.name: quasi
modify_link_terms.example: quasi una fantasia almost a fantasia

modify_link_terms.name: senza
modify_link_terms.example: senza pedale: without using the pedal

modify_link_terms.name: subito, sub.
modify_link_terms.example: subito pp, which instructs the player to suddenly drop to pianissimo as an effect

history.name: Composer of Invention in C Major
polyphonic texture
history.definition: combination of 2 or more melody lines, also known as contrapuntal texture or counterpoint

history.name: homophonic texture
history.definition: a single line of melody supported by harmonic accompaniment

history.name: motive
history.definition: a short melodic or rhythmic fragment used to build a melody

history.name: invention
history.definition: keyboard composition in polyphonic texture based on imitation

history.name: imitation
history.definition: repitition of the same motive, in another voice or part

history.name: sequence
history.definition: a motive or phrase that is repeated at a higher or lower pitch in the same voice

history.name: concerto grosso
history.definition: a Baroque orchestral work in 3 movements (fast-slow-fast). A concertino is contrasted with a ripieno

history.name: ritornello form
history.definition: a form often used as the 1st and 3rd movements of a concerto grosso. The openning ritornello is repeated throughout the movement
